text:
frank: quick pitch — build an org-key broker shim that exchanges org API keys for short-lived project tokens. goal: avoid urgent customer rekeying and enable project-scoped RBAC. comments?

nina: sounds good. must keep audit lineage (original key id), and ensure revocation is fast.

oscar: agree. propose default token ttl=300s, optional refresh flow for server-side jobs (1h). include `audit_id` and `x-delegation-id` on downstream calls.

frank: mapping storage idea: customer-signed YAML in S3, validated by shim (ed25519). shim caches and supports admin `POST /reload`.

nina: revocation plan: pub/sub revocation events + small in-memory blacklist for immediate rejects. mapping version `kv.ver` in tokens to detect stale mappings.

oscar: fallback semantics: circuit-breaker -> legacy behavior but annotate `x-auth-fallback:legacy` and emit `auth.fallbacks` event. ops must alert on that.

infra-bot: deploy-check: canary in two regions, per-instance RPS cap 200, global burst cap 2k, circuit-breaker policy required.

sec: security notes: threat model (impersonation, replay, signing key compromise). require HSM for signing keys, TLS everywhere, pen-test before public rollout.

frank: migration steps: 1) internal FF + simulate only, 2) telemetry mode, 3) closed beta per-customer, 4) gradual opt-in + 12mo deprecation window.

nina: I'll draft mapping grammar and CLI helpers.

oscar: I'll own telemetry + ops runbook.

frank: thanks — I'll write the short RFC and tag @nina @oscar @sec for review. meeting Friday 11 to finalize TTLs.
